_readme: EV-1 - the badge->check registry (trust-model DESIGN section 9, LOCKED).
THE RULE: trust can only be claimed where a machine can re-derive the claim. Every
Guardian claim term appearing anywhere in the declared `doc_layer` must be accounted
for HERE, in exactly one of three buckets, and `validate_skills.check_badge_registry`
walks BOTH directions on every commit:
forward  - a doc-layer line carrying a claim term that no entry covers FAILS
(the uncited-badge direction: facade regrowth is a validator failure,
not a future hand-audit finding).
backward - a registry entry whose file/anchor no longer resolves FAILS, and a
`badges` entry whose cited check is dead FAILS (the cited-but-dead
direction). The registry-vs-tree precedent is
`validate_skills.check_reuse_claims_producers_exist`.
THE THREE BUCKETS:
badges              - a real Guardian trust/enforcement claim WITH a live check id.
pending_graduation  - a real claim whose check is NOT yet live. Carries the honest
non-claim Guardian grade it must be read at today plus the
route that will make it true. This is the bucket the T6-T11
facade rows sit in until their wiring lands.
non_claims          - the term appears but asserts no trust: a vocabulary
definition, a heading, a negation ("never render it as
Verified"), a different vocabulary that collides on the word
(reuse-claims' `Verified` class), or ordinary English.
Each carries a WRITTEN reason. This is an escape hatch by
construction - the reason field and the commit are what make
using it a loud act rather than a quiet one (the
PROTOCOL_EXEMPT bargain, stated not designed away).
THE GRADUATION MECHANISM (how a facade row becomes an honest badge):
a `pending_graduation` row graduates by being MOVED into `badges` by the task that
lands its wiring, in the same commit, gaining a `check` that resolves live. It
cannot graduate any other way: `badges` refuses an entry without a live check, and
DELETING the row instead leaves its badge site uncovered in the tree, which fails
the forward direction by name. Downgrading it stays legal and honest - move it to
`non_claims` only if the site stops making a claim at all.
CHECK-ID GRAMMAR: the CLOSED three-form evidence grammar, unchanged and not
re-implemented - `artifact:<repo-relative-path>` | `test:<pytest-node-id>` |
`probe:<registered-name>`, parsed and guarded by
`evidence_grammar.compile_declaration` (tools/evidence_grammar.py). Paths are
REPO-relative, matching the PLAN's `evidence:` declarations. Liveness is checked on
top of the grammar: a `test:` node's file must exist AND define the named test, an
`artifact:` path must exist, and a `probe:` name must be registered in
tools/probe_registry.json with status `active` - a `declared-before-active` probe is
NOT a live check for a Verified badge, it is a `pending_graduation` route.
WHY THIS FILE IS NOT FINGERPRINTED: it is a registry that grows with the codebase,
the same structural exemption `protocol/config.md` and `protocol/exec-safety.md`
earn in PROTOCOL_FINGERPRINTS. The risk here is a MISSING entry, which the forward
direction already covers; a digest would impose a re-approval per routine addition,
which is exactly how blind re-approval gets trained.
HONEST RESIDUALS, stated rather than designed away:
1. Claim-term matching is CASE-SENSITIVE and literal. A site that spells the grade
some other way is invisible to this check. Guarding the Guardian vocabulary is
what EV-1 scopes; guarding arbitrary trust-flavoured prose is judgment and stays
with the reviewer and the grounding gate.
2. Classification into the three buckets is HUMAN judgment, committed as data. The
check enforces that every site is classified and that every cited check is live;
it does not and cannot decide that a classification was honest.
3. Guardian DOWNGRADES (`Honor-system`, `Dormant`, `Broken`) are deliberately NOT
claim terms. EV-1 guards the claim of verification; an honest downgrade asserts
no trust and needs no citation.
_doc_layer_note: The declared claim-bearing surface: the shipped contract layer (protocol/, docs/,
skills/, modules/, the root docs) plus the two named .planning artifacts that carry
standing Guardian marks - BACKLOG.md (the section 6.6 truth-status rule: "BUILT" is
legal ONLY with the Verified evidence citation) and the promise audit (the row set
wave 9 relabels). The REST of .planning/** is deliberately out of scope: grill
ledgers, observation logs and design records are an ACCOUNT of a discussion, not a
standing claim to a reader, and pulling them in would make the registry a transcript
index. Narrowing this list is a visible edit to a committed file, by design.

badges.note: The `plan` governor rung is graded Verified because the mint REFUSES on an unfrozen plan - the cited test exercises that refusal (`governs='plan'` against a draft plan -> 'plan rung unmet'), so the grade is re-derivable rather than asserted.

The healthy default level. The cited test pins it to RESILIENCE_LOCAL and proves the level cannot be lifted by a worker-authored record - the failure mode that would turn this Partially-verified into a manufactured Verified.
DESIGN section 6.2's "never the config flag", enforced in code. The cited test is the one that folds RECORDED outcomes and refuses the flag as an input.

R-ENF (guardian-relabel-pass, Loop D): the README:89 'workers structurally cannot drift' facade graduates because the dispatch seam (W3) mints a per-task record and the fail-closed pre-hook (Loop C) DENIES a record-less Agent launch at PreToolUse. The cited test drives that recordless-launch deny. The claim carries its own install-gated / Honor-system-where-not-installed qualifier on the same line, so the badge is Verified WHERE INSTALLED, not an unqualified always-live claim.

R-ROLE (guardian-relabel-pass, Loop D): config.md:32's 'roles wired, code-enforced, not advisory' graduates because role->rung resolution is consumed at mint by the seam governor (kata_dispatch._ROLE_CLASS / GOVERNOR_GRADE, role-class-scoped fail-closed rung). The cited test proves the mint wires the role resolver.
